A hyper-detailed, photoreal hero product render of a premium hardware device, like a flagship launch image from a top industrial design studio: A long horizontal control unit machined from thick brushed aluminium rests on the glossy black floor: a central landscape screen set in a black glass panel, a large knurled dial at each end.

The output is one single photograph, landscape 16:9.

Composition A, centred and symmetric: the design surface sits on the centre line, square to the camera, with even space on both sides; strong verticals and horizontals run parallel to the frame. Shot: Camera straight on, about 10 degrees above, 100mm lens, so a sliver of the top face shows its thickness. The unit spans about 80 percent of the frame width on the centre line; the screen fills about 40 percent of the frame width, sharp, square-on; fine engraved tick-mark scales ring each dial; a row of tiny LED dots sits under the screen; a recessed hex screw in each corner; the floor mirrors it softly. Nobody is in frame.

Place: A deep black studio with a glossy black floor that mirrors the device softly; nothing else in the frame but the device.

Light: Large strip softboxes from above and both sides draw long, clean gradient reflections down the metal; a thin cool rim light traces every edge; tiny specular glints on screws, knurling and chamfers; the rest falls to black.

Palette and grade: Neutral and cool: brushed aluminium, satin steel, matte black and graphite on pure black; the screen a clean neutral white. The same grade on every image of the collection.

Real: this is a product mockup render, so the screen is the hero: large, sharp and fully readable, glowing evenly. The device is dense with believable engineering detail: fine brushed-metal grain, diamond-cut chamfers, knurled edges, recessed hex screws, hairline seams, tiny speaker perforations, small status LED dots, engraved tick marks, rubber gaskets; every part has real thickness and depth, never a flat cut-out. The design surface faces the camera almost square-on, within about 15 degrees, so it reads flat and undistorted; its four edges run parallel to the edges of the photograph, a true rectangle, never a trapezoid or keystone; flat things on a table are shot from nearly straight above. Only the device named is in frame.

Design surface: THE SCREEN SHOWS A PLAIN WHITE FULL-SCREEN IMAGE, evenly lit edge to edge, crisp corners inside its black border, nothing on it.

Finish: Path-traced and razor sharp: physically accurate metal, glass and rubber, crisp micro-detail, deep blacks, soft depth of field only on the floor reflection; it looks like a real flagship product launch render, never flat, never bland.

Avoid: logos, letters, numbers or brand names anywhere, any image, icon or text on the screen, any object other than the device, a flat, bland, simplified or low-detail look, a cheap plastic, cartoon or toy look.
